reviews.author: K
reviews.text: Sponsored // I am leaving a review of my visit to the Common Unique showroom near Hongik University Station. In fact, there were so many women's clothing stores in Hongdae that I was worried about where to go, but this store was often seen on social media and was recommended by an acquaintance, so I decided to visit it. The store was very conveniently located, about a 5-minute walk from Exit 1 of Hongik University Station, and it had a cafe-like atmosphere from the outside, so I had high expectations even before entering. The interior was neatly organized and the clothes were nicely arranged by color and item, so it was fun to choose. Above all, there are many daily items such as basic t-shirts and slacks, but the prices are reasonable, so I was able to shop without burden. I purchased a white T-shirt and a nice-fitting denim skirt, and the quality was much better than the price, so I was very satisfied. It was also nice that items like shoes and bags were available so you could complete your outfit in one go. The fitting room was spacious and the lighting was warm, so it was good for taking pictures of the items worn. The staff also kindly recommended sizes and outfits, so I was able to shop comfortably. Overall, I was satisfied with both the store atmosphere and the quality of the clothes, and I think it would be a good place to stop by when shopping in Yeonnam-dong. Personally, I would like to recommend this place among women's clothing stores in Hongdae because it offers both cost-effectiveness and sensibility.

reviews.author: Gun Heo
reviews.text: It's been a year since I went to Novaskin, and this Hongdae dermatology clinic really changed my skin life. Actually, my skin was so bad that even makeup couldn't cover it up. Acne was the norm, as well as acne marks, pores, and dull skin tone... I felt depressed every time I looked in the mirror. Even when I met friends, I always had to put on heavy makeup, and I still didn't have confidence because of my skin. At first, I went to a dermatologist near my house, but it wasn't very effective and it was expensive, so I quit. Then, when I moved to Hongdae for work, I looked into Hongdae dermatology clinics, and a senior at the company recommended Novaskin, so I went there. During the first consultation, the director looked at my skin and said, “It will take some time, but it can get better.” Those words really helped me a lot. Meanwhile, at other dermatologists' clinics, they just said, "Get this treatment," but here they explained why my skin was like this and in what order I should treat it. Treatment was planned as a long-term plan. The first three months were focused on controlling inflammation and normalizing skin turnover, the next three months were on scar and pigment treatment, and now it's the maintenance phase. To be honest, I was skeptical at first, but after two months, no new acne appeared. After four months, my friends started asking me, “Why has your skin improved so much these days?” Now I can confidently go out without makeup. I really don't know how long this is. What's great about Novaskin is that the director really thinks from the patient's perspective. Please do not recommend expensive procedures, but find the best method within your budget. And if it doesn't work, be honest and say, "I don't think this will suit your skin type." The staff are also very friendly, and are flexible enough to change reservations or anything like that. Please provide detailed information on post-procedure care, and if you have any questions, please kindly answer them via KakaoTalk. The location is really good too. 3 minutes from Exit 6 of Hongik University Station? It's close to work, and there are many restaurants and cafes nearby, so it's great for getting treatment and meeting friends. The price... honestly, I wouldn't say it's cheap, but considering the effects, it's reasonable enough. And if you buy a package, they give you a lot of discounts and hold frequent events. If you are really worried about dermatology in Hongdae, please get a consultation at Novaskin. It will really be a source of hope for those who have been struggling with their skin like me!

reviews.author: Junho Kim
reviews.text: I've actually been to a lot of dermatologists, and I think Novaskin is the best dermatology clinic in Hongdae. I had a lot of skin problems because I had acne, pores, and pigmentation. I've been to several dermatologists for almost 4 years since my first year of college, but some gave only mediocre consultations and only recommended expensive treatments, and some didn't work... I was really stressed out. Then, when I moved to Hongdae last year, I discovered Novaskin. At first, I just went to a dermatologist near my house for a casual consultation, but I felt completely different from the first consultation. The director looked at my skin condition very closely. He explained step by step why my skin problem occurred and in what order I should treat it. And the best thing was that there was no excessive recommendation at all. I told him my budget and he came up with the best plan within it. “This needs to be done right now, and you can do this later when you have some free time.” He said so honestly that I really gained trust. Treatment started with controlling the inflammation. I was prescribed medication and received laser treatment once every two weeks, but after a month, almost no new acne appeared. After that, I underwent treatment for scars and pigmentation, and after receiving this treatment consistently for about 3 months, it definitely improved. I've been going for 6 months now, and everyone around me asks me if my skin has improved. My friends, my part-time job colleagues, and even friends I meet on the street ask me things like, “Hey, what did you put on your skin? It’s completely improved,” and I feel really proud every time. Haha. Another good thing about Novaskin is that they have a really good reservation system. You can make a reservation through KakaoTalk, and the time is fast so there is almost no waiting time. At other dermatologists, you often have to wait an hour for an appointment, but that's not the case here. And since the treatment room is a private space, privacy is well maintained. The staff are all friendly, and they even send me a text message telling me how to take care of myself after the procedure. The location is right in front of Hongik University Station, so it's perfect for going after school, and there are many cafes nearby, so it's great to get treatment and have tea with friends. The price is really reasonable too. I was worried that it would be burdensome because I am a student, but they provide a student discount and it is cheaper if you buy it as a package. It's a level I can easily afford with my part-time salary. I highly recommend Novaskin to those who are looking for a dermatologist in Hongdae, especially those who have lost confidence because of their skin like me. Dermatology is my life!

reviews.author: Retro Man
reviews.text:
I went to the Modeman Yeouido branch and put the clothes I was wearing on the hanger on display for a moment to try them on. But perhaps my clothes placed on top of the products on display were annoying, and there were only two groups of customers, including me, so it wasn't too busy, but the waitress hit my clothes on purpose, causing them to fall on the floor? You thought I couldn’t see, right? And you said you would move my clothes without even shaking them out? I found out later that they were stacked on chairs where employees sit behind the counter...? No, my clothes cost close to 1 million won. If it's a customer's clothes, I should hang them on a hanger, but should I store them by crumpling them on a chair? If I were you and the hanging clothes bothered you, I would naturally lead you by saying, “I’ll hang them on a hanger for you.” Anyway, how many minutes did it bother you that much?

1. There were about 4 employees selling clothes worth over 1 million won, and I was surprised by the number of employees compared to the store.
2. I was quite displeased with the employee's subtle rudeness.

If you buy clothes that cost more than 1 million won, you need to have employees who are appropriate for their level. In the hospitality industry, they wear hats and things like that... It was pathetic to see employees who didn't have the basics of good clothes... The store manager should be trained on customer service, but there was no training at all, and I hope to use college graduates in the future, and it would be best to just sell in an online shop or close the Yeouido branch...

reviews.text: On September 28th, I was shopping at Top Ten in Hongdae with my family. The kids started running around and giggling, but after about 5 minutes, an employee named Shinhae started yelling at me. I didn't say anything to my husband who was next to me. I held my two-year-old daughter tightly to prevent her from crying loudly. Then the employee came back and harassed me and warned me in an unfriendly manner. I felt embarrassed and offended at the thought of being discriminated against in a children's clothing store (because I looked Asian). The employees, including the manager, did not apologize (although they made the excuse that they did not understand English) and kept yelling at me to "Be quiet and don't make noise." My family came to Seoul to relax, not to receive parenting education from Top Ten. I think the staff needs to be properly trained on cultural appropriation and tourist service. cu famous for ramen library
The staff was very friendly and helpful.
And there were rare ramen items that are hard to find these days (seaweed soup ramen), but alcoholic beverages were not available inside.
The container fee of 1,800 won must be paid separately.
In the case of Japanese ramen, the thick noodles are different from Korean ramen because they require a lot of water, so the cooking method is different.
Personally, I went there out of curiosity, but I don't think I'll go again.

Convenience stores are just that, a ramen shop itself.
It's open 24 hours, so you can stop by any time. Although there isn't a lot of space for eating, it's spacious and equipped with several cooking utensils.
There are a lot of ramen bags, but you have to buy the container separately, which is comparable to the price of ramen, so if you really need to eat ramen, I recommend cup ramen, but if you want to feel emotional when you come to a place like this, you have no choice.
Anyway, it’s a convenience store with an interesting concept.

reviews.author: Mana Salem
reviews.text:
Okay, I finally went to the CU Ramen Library in Hongdae that everyone was talking about. To cut the hype, it's not a fancy restaurant, but it's a truly unique and satisfying experience.

The key here is this concept. Once inside, it's designed like an atmospheric, minimalist library, but instead of books, the shelves are stacked with every kind of instant ramen imaginable. From classic Shin Ramyun to little-known local brands, and even ramen from around the world. Just pick up the basket, look through the “drawers”, and choose the ramen you want.

This process is half the fun. After choosing your noodles, you go to the counter and select the spiciness level and additional ingredients like cheese or eggs, and the ramen will be prepared in a proper kitchen. I chose vegan, spicy level 1 and added one more egg.

What are the results? It was a steaming bowl of perfect comfort food. It tasted exactly like the ramen I made at home at 2 a.m., but it tasted even better because I didn't have to wash the pot. The soup was warm and flavorful, and the eggs melted and were really delicious.

The space is small and there are always a lot of people, so I think we'll have to share a table. It is a noisy and lively place, so it is not a suitable place for a quiet date. But this fast, cheap, and Instagram-friendly restaurant is the perfect choice because it turns a solo snack into a social gathering.

reviews.text:
You can reach this store just a short walk from Hongik University Station or Hongdo Shopping Center.

This place sells as many as 225 types of noodles and ramen, and you can create your own ramen by choosing as many toppings as you want.

There's so much to choose from that it can be a little difficult to choose, but once you've chosen all the toppings you want, you'll receive a barcoded bowl. After payment, of course. Now just place all the ingredients in a bowl and cook according to the instructions.

There is a countertop nearby. First scan the barcode and press the start button. In just a few minutes, your own ramen will be ready.

If you come to Seoul, be sure to stop by this amazing ramen restaurant!

reviews.text: A place where you can rent equipment needed for photography and videography. They have quite a variety of equipment. reviews.author: ZZIM!
reviews.text:
It was so unfriendly. Not even 1 star is worth it. I clearly told them in advance that I was a student and a foreigner, and received an answer that rental was possible. However, when I visited the store on the day of rental, I was told that rental was not possible. The reason was that the person in charge of renting the car was a foreigner and a student. I think it's unfair to suddenly be treated that way even though I was told at first that it didn't matter. Even the way he was guided was very unfriendly. I think the staff's service spirit is lacking.
What's even more absurd is the response afterward. When another person in charge called to find out the truth, the response was completely different from the one given to the visitor. I think this is clear discrimination against foreigners. I don't know what the staff's training methods are like, but I really don't want to visit again.
I hope you know that you contributed greatly to the enormous delay in shooting my film. Aside from my own movies, how many other shoots have you ruined? I'm really impressed.

reviews.author: claim (claim)
reviews.text:
A place that anyone who takes pictures would never go. Don't go.
Obviously I warned you. SL Allent used to be nice when it was small and cozy at Boutique Monaco in Gangnam, but if I go here now, I'll go to Han Rental. The equipment there is old and you have to rent it in bulk or there is no schedule.
It's not as absurd as this.
If you unravel the story that happened here, it's really....
A place I will never do business with again as the last filming took place last year.

1. CF memory is cheap, so data is lost.

2. A place where extension of rental time is absolutely not possible. There are many variables in filming, so sometimes it is impossible to meet the 8 o'clock deadline. However, other rental stores tell you to come safely as it is okay to be late if the weather is bad, but this is a place where the part-timer screams and pressures you as if you think that your work time is important.

I even fell and tore my leg while running through the snow to meet the deadline here, and I still can't forget the attitude of the employee who quickly asked for equipment rather than asking the person who was bleeding to see if he was okay.

3. I received production support from Pickp a long time ago, so I started using their equipment.
The baby was omitted, and the lighting was also omitted by Alba.

I'm still angry when I think about the fact that I missed filming because I rented it here. I'm not going. There are many places to rent besides here.
